policy_specific_actions_2:
Strengthen health research for evidence-informed policy-making and self-sufficiency in 
health technology 
Robust health research ensures the best available evidence to guide and inform policymakers in the selection of possible strategies to achieve health system goals. It can also lead to self-sufficiency in health technology by ensuring that health investments are prioritized for high-value innovations  including traditional, complementary, and alternative health care products and services  that improve the quality of life of Filipinos. As such, promoting institutionalization of decision-making based on health research, development, and innovation (RDI) will be a priority. Increased, dedicated, and conditioned funding will focus on health RDI that: (a) translate basic health research into practical aspects; (b) promote low-cost and climate-resilient innovations for remote populations and vulnerable sectors based on projected health needs and service delivery gaps in the medium term; and (c) improve capacity for high quality local vaccine and medicine development and production (See Chapter 8).

Policy 1 specifically targets innovation and research on AMR, aiming to build a supportive environment and disseminate knowledge in this specialized area. Policy 2, while broader in scope, aims to strengthen health research for evidence-informed policymaking and capacity building. Together, they address the gap of limited investment in AMR research by promoting targeted and general research enhancements that mutually support the development of critical health technologies and innovations.
implementation_interpretation: Policy 1 implements a targeted AMR research agenda with specific measures such as establishing databases, upgrading IT systems, and coordinating with research stakeholders. Policy 2 strengthens overall health research infrastructure and enhances funding for high-value innovations. The strengthened research capacity and resource mobilization under Policy 2 can directly support the specialized initiatives of Policy 1, while the focused outputs from Policy 1 can contribute to the broader health research objectives of Policy 2, creating a synergistic relationship.

implementation_interpretation: Policy 1's mechanisms for stable funding, dynamic monitoring, social security, and infrastructure support create a secure foundation for the industrial diversification efforts of Policy 2. In turn, Policy 2's development of integrated primary, secondary, and tertiary rural industries, improved logistics, and farmer shareholding schemes generate sustainable incomes and enterprise opportunities that reinforce the poverty-prevention and consolidation goals of Policy 1. This reciprocal reinforcement makes each policy easier to implement.

policy_specific_actions_2:
I. Gender equality and development of women 
The Program for the Development of Chinese Women will be implemented for a continuously improved environment for women’s development, in which women are able to exercise their rights, participate in economic and social development, and benefit from the development outcomes on an equal basis in accordance with the law. Women’s access to health services will be ensured, in particular to comprehensive prevention and treatment of cervical and breast cancers and relevant relief policies. Women will be guaranteed to have equal right to education and see an increase in their number of years of schooling as well as their overall ability and quality. Rural women’s land rights and interests will be protected. Women will be guaranteed to enjoy equal political rights and largely participate in social affairs and democratic management. Mechanisms for assessing gender equality in laws and policies will be implemented. And the gender-specific data collection system will be improved. Each policy thus facilitates the other's roll-out and uptake.

It is important to ensure that personal income grows in step with economic growth and that workers’ compensation rises in tandem with the increase in labor productivity. It is also important to continue to increase the income of low-income groups while expanding the size of the middle-income group in an effort to bring prosperity to all.

We will improve the interest linkage mechanism, and ensure farmers share more benefits from the growth of industries by “turning resources into assets, funds into shares, and farmers into shareholders”.
policy_specific_actions_2:
I. More opportunities to increase income 
The system in which distribution according to work is dominant and a variety of modes of distribution coexist will see an increase in the proportion of labor remuneration in the primary distribution. To better decide and increase wages, as well as secure the payment, it is needed to improve the mechanism for developing the minimum wage standard and wage guidelines, and determining wages through collective discussion. Efforts will be made to improve the mechanism whereby remuneration for various factors of production is determined by the market, and explore ways to increase the income of low-and-middle-income groups through their rights to use and benefit from land, capital, and other production factors, so as to improve distribution policies and systems based on production factors. In state-owned enterprises, the market-oriented salary distribution mechanism will be improved, and the performance-based evaluation system of employees will be implemented across the board. In public institutions, reform aims to improve the salary system to reflect job performance, position level, and job category. Standards will be set for labor dispatch and employment to ensure equal pay for equal work. More 
 channels will be opened to increase the property income of urban and rural residents, including raising the proportion of farmers’ share in land value-added revenue, improving the dividend system of listed companies, and developing more innovative financial products to meet the needs of type wealth management. The system by which state capital gains are turned over to public finance will be improved so as to increase public spending in people’s wellbeing. 
II. Expanding the rank of middle-income earners 
An initiative to expand the rank of the middle-income earners and consistently increase its proportion will be launched, with the focus on graduates from regular universities and vocational schools, skilled workers, and migrant workers. Support will be provided for graduates from universities and vocational schools to help them find jobs, in particular those suiting their academic background. Efforts will be made to offer more opportunities for skilled workers, especially those in non-public economic organizations, social organizations, and freelance professionals and technicians, to apply for professional titles and qualification certificates for promotion, raising their benefits and social status. A program to develop competent farmers will be launched to help them use agricultural and rural resources and modern operation methods to increase their income. Policies will be devised to support small and micro startups, and support groups such as self-employed individuals and workers in flexible employment, to embark on the journey of prosperity through hard work. 
III. A more rational wealth and income redistribution mechanism 
The distribution pattern of income and wealth will be improved, benefiting from more intense and accurate adjustments to taxation, social security, and transfer payments, and the role of charity in the third distribution. Measures will be taken to advance the direct tax system by improving the system for taxing personal income on the basis of both adjusted gross income and specific types of income, and strengthening tax regulation and supervision of high-income individuals. With dynamically adjusted standards in response to the basic needs, social security benefits and services will become fairer and more accessible. The income distribution order will be well-regulated to protect legitimate income, regulate excessive income in a reasonable manner, ban illegal income, and curb income obtained by means of monopoly and unfair competition. A sound system of information on personal income and property will be established and the modern payment and income monitoring system will be perfected.
objective_interpretation: Both SDG-02 and SDG-10 aim to improve individual socio-demographic factors by raising incomes, reducing poverty, and sharing economic gains. SDG-02 does this by diversifying and upgrading rural livelihoods, turning farmers into stakeholders in emerging rural industries. SDG-10 complements this by ensuring fair wage setting, stronger social protection, and progressive redistribution, all of which bolster individual economic security. Together, they push the same driver--individual socioeconomic status--in a positive direction, generating cumulative benefits for AMR risk factors linked to low income and limited livelihood options.
implementation_interpretation: SDG-02's development of rural industries, property-rights trading, and shareholding mechanisms creates new avenues for farmers to earn property income, directly supporting SDG-10's objective to increase returns from land and capital for low- and middle-income groups. Conversely, SDG-10's reforms to wage setting, minimum wage standards, and property-income channels (e.g. land value-added revenue, dividend systems) provide the institutional and fiscal framework that ensures the economic gains generated under SDG-02 are equitably distributed, thus reinforcing the uptake and impact of rural economic diversification measures.

 channels will be opened to increase the property income of urban and rural residents, including raising the proportion of farmers’ share in land value-added revenue, improving the dividend system of listed companies, and developing more innovative financial products to meet the needs of type wealth management. An initiative to expand the rank of the middle-income earners and consistently increase its proportion will be launched, with the focus on graduates from regular universities and vocational schools, skilled workers, and migrant workers. policy_strategic_objective_1:
Basic Rights and Interests of Women, Children, and People with Disabilities 
Gender equality, child development, and disability care, among others, are key components of our national policy to protect the rights of disadvantaged groups, including women, children, and people with disabilities, and give them opportunities to thrive.
policy_strategic_objective_2: More opportunities to increase income
policy_specific_actions_1:
I. Gender equality and development of women 
The Program for the Development of Chinese Women will be implemented for a continuously improved environment for women’s development, in which women are able to exercise their rights, participate in economic and social development, and benefit from the development outcomes on an equal basis in accordance with the law. Women’s access to health services will be ensured, in particular to comprehensive prevention and treatment of cervical and breast cancers and relevant relief policies. Women will be guaranteed to have equal right to education and see an increase in their number of years of schooling as well as their overall ability and quality. Women will be guaranteed to enjoy equal economic rights and interests, be free from gender discrimination in employment, and enjoy law-based maternity leave and maternity allowance. Rural women’s land rights and interests will be protected. Women will be guaranteed to enjoy equal political rights and largely participate in social affairs and democratic management. Mechanisms for assessing gender equality in laws and policies will be implemented. And the gender-specific data collection system will be improved. Efforts will be made to ensure quality care services for women left behind in rural areas, and crack down on illegal and criminal acts infringing upon the personal rights of women and girls.
policy_specific_actions_2: The system in which distribution according to work is dominant and a variety of modes of distribution coexist will see an increase in the proportion of labor remuneration in the primary distribution. To better decide and increase wages, as well as secure the payment, it is needed to improve the mechanism for developing the minimum wage standard and wage guidelines, and determining wages through collective discussion. Efforts will be made to improve the mechanism whereby remuneration for various factors of production is determined by the market, and explore ways to increase the income of low-and-middle-income groups through their rights to use and benefit from land, capital, and other production factors, so as to improve distribution policies and systems based on production factors. In state-owned enterprises, the market-oriented salary distribution mechanism will be improved, and the performance-based evaluation system of employees will be implemented across the board. In public institutions, reform aims to improve the salary system to reflect job performance, position level, and job category. Standards will be set for labor dispatch and employment to ensure equal pay for equal work. More channels will be opened to increase the property income of urban and rural residents, including raising the proportion of farmers’ share in land value-added revenue, improving the dividend system of listed companies, and developing more innovative financial products to meet the needs of type wealth management. objective_interpretation: Both policies address socio-cultural determinants of AMR by improving social equity and empowerment. implementation_interpretation: Policy 1's measures to ensure women's equal economic rights, labor participation and data on gender equity create a stronger foundation for the income-boosting mechanisms of Policy 2 (e.g. women can better access collective wage setting, minimum wage standards, land-value revenue and financial products). Conversely, Policy 2's improvements in wages, property incomes and social welfare finance reinforce women's economic empowerment and equal treatment in the labor market targeted by Policy 1. This reciprocal reinforcement makes each policy easier to implement when the other is in place.

Enhancement of career education and vocational education
policy_strategic_objective_2: Promote gender equality and women's empowerment
policy_specific_actions_1:
Give support to children in completing elementary and secondary education to ensure equal opportunities in education. Revise and implement the national curriculum standards to provide children with a sufficient level of education throughout the country and help them foster competency required for the new era. Also to this end, improve the quality and abilities of teachers and enhance the allocation of teacher and other staffs. 
In addition to raising basic and general abilities that provide a foundation for social and vocational independence, we will prepare opportunities in which students can correspond to the mobilization of the labor market and gain practical and academic knowledge and skills throughout their lifetimes. 
In order to achieve this, enhancement of career education, improvement of internship projects, and collaboration between education and employment are required to avoid job mismatching.
policy_specific_actions_2:
Based on the National Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security (formulated in 2015), promote the participation of women in decision-making processes both in Japan and abroad, and give consideration to the human rights of women and gender perspective when tackling challenges for peace and security
Based on the issue-specific development policies to support women (set in 2016), support developing countries in attaining Sustainable Development Goal 5 with a focus on: (1) promoting women’s and girls’ rights; (2) improving an enabling environment for women and girls to reach their full potentials; and (3) advancing women’s leadership in politics, economy and other public fields.
objective_interpretation: Both SDG-04 (enhancing education and vocational skills) and SDG-05 (promoting gender equality and women's empowerment) act on the individual socio-demographic drivers of AMR by strengthening personal capacities--education raises awareness, critical thinking and responsible behaviors around antimicrobial use, while gender equality ensures women (who often manage type health) are empowered to make informed health decisions. By improving the socio-demographic characteristics of the population in complementary ways, they collectively reduce vulnerability to misuse of antimicrobials.
implementation_interpretation: Efforts to enhance education quality and access build a foundation that directly supports gender equality--e.g., improving teacher competencies and curriculum standards includes gender-responsive pedagogy, while career education and internships increase women's participation in the workforce and leadership. Conversely, women's empowerment initiatives facilitate girls' and women's enrollment and retention in education, ensuring resources allocated through SDG-04 reach female learners. Thus, each policy's implementation reinforces and eases the implementation of the other.

policy_specific_actions_2:
Working-style reform represents the biggest challenge to be met across the board to create a society in which all citizens are dynamically engaged. Accordingly, implement measures to provide workers with more working style options by improving working conditions of non-regular workers including the achievement of equal pay for equal work, reducing overtime work and total working hours, and fostering the employment of older workers by encouraging companies to increase the retirement age to 65 and offer their employees ongoing employment even after reaching that age.

Based on Japan’s Plan for Dynamic Engagement of All Citizens, enhance the execution of the legal regulations and also start reexamining how to regulate overtime work approved under the so called “36 agreement,” which is made between an employer and the labor union in accordance with Article 36 of the Labor Standards Act to allow the employer to extend the working hours of employees without limit. 

Based on Japan’s Plan for Dynamic Engagement of All Citizens, foster the steady implementation of the Act for Employment Promotion etc. of Youth (enacted in 2015) and foster the employment of young people to provide them with more opportunities to effectively demonstrate their abilities.
objective_interpretation: Both policies act on individual socio-demographic drivers of AMR by improving education, employability and working conditions. SDG-04 raises education levels and career readiness, fostering health literacy and social empowerment, while SDG-08 reduces overwork and promotes stable youth employment, improving socioeconomic status and the capacity for responsible health behaviors. Together they push the same driver--strengthening individual socio-demographic resilience--toward reduced AMR risk.
implementation_interpretation: SDG-04's enhancement of career education, internships and school-industry collaboration creates a pipeline of skilled, motivated young workers, which directly supports SDG-08's youth employment measures and working-style reforms by providing qualified candidates and established training pathways. Conversely, SDG-08's improved labor practices and expanded employment opportunities give students clear prospects for workforce entry, reinforcing the uptake and effectiveness of SDG-04's vocational and career-education initiatives.

policy_strategic_objective_2: Implementation of the Action Plan for Strengthening Measures on Emerging Infectious Diseases
policy_specific_actions_1:
Regarding infection prevention and control (IPC), expand activities in cooperation with regional hospitals and 
related organizations (clinics, pharmacies, nursing care facilities, public health centers, prefectural and municipal public health institutes, etc.), develop concrete activity models of a comprehensive regional infection prevention and control network, and support its sequential establishment all over the country
policy_specific_actions_2: Based on the Action Plan for Strengthening Measures on Emerging Infectious Diseases, aim to create the society with strenghtned systems to counter infectious diseases by establishing improved domestic systems, including health and medical services, test and research systems, and human resource base for infectious diseases.
objective_interpretation: Both policies seek to strengthen infection prevention and control and overall health system capacity to reduce infection and colonization by resistant bacteria in humans. Policy AMR-03 focuses on implementing IPC measures and regional cooperation to prevent the spread of resistant organisms in care settings, while SDG-03's Action Plan strengthens domestic systems--health services, testing, research, and workforce--against emerging infectious diseases. Together they push the shared driver (human infection by resistant bacteria) in the same direction by building complementary capabilities and infrastructure.
implementation_interpretation: The IPC network and regional cooperation structures established under AMR-03 provide existing platforms, data flows, and partnerships that SDG-03 can leverage to roll out enhanced testing, research, and workforce initiatives. Conversely, the improved health service systems, laboratory capacities, and trained personnel created through SDG-03 bolster the reach, quality, and sustainability of the IPC activities under AMR-03, creating a positive feedback loop for both implementations.

policy_strategic_objective_2:
Steady implementation of the G7 Ise-Shima Vision for Global Health 
Contribution towards strengthening the global health architecture and relevant systems 
Support for the enhancement of the WHO’s emergency response unit and to the Organization’s emergency response activities
Support for the World Bank’s Pandemic Emergency Financing Facility (PEF) for strengthening response to public health emergencies 
Promotion of UHC and strengthening preparedness and prevention against public health emergencies in collaboration with the World Bank
policy_specific_actions_1: Establish a response system to a large-scale outbreak which causes a serious shortage of human resources by  dispatching experts throughout the country regarding epidemiological investigations, clinical management, and public health responses, as appropriate. In addition, the deployment of local infectious disease specialists will be enhanced during normal times, and the response support system from the national level to the local level will be strengthened
policy_specific_actions_2:
Foster the implementation of the G7 Ise-Shima Vision for Global Health, which the G7 countries announced at the Ise-Shima Summit, and contribute to the attainment of Goal 3 and other SDGs. 

Make contribution at international discussions on the global health architecture to improve emergency responses to public health emergencies, thereby contributing to strengthening the architecture. 

Make financial contribution to CFE(Contigency Fund for Emergencies） to improve its initial response in case of emergency and in the event of the outbreak of infectious diseases. Give support to the establishment of the WHO’s health risk management system, thereby contributing to the enhancement of responses to and preparations against public health crises in each country across the world. 

The PEF is a funding mechanism for timely disbursement of financial resourses in response to pandemics by utilizing insurance instruments. As a main donor of the PEF, the Japanese government makes financial contribution and engage in appropriate management of the PEF in order to strengthen and accelerate response to public health emergencies. 

The Japanese government supports for acceleration of UHC and strengthening preparedness and prevention against public health emergencies in developing countries in collaboration with the World Bank and the WHO through the following measures: Support actual implementation of ""UHC in Africa"", which was announced during TICAD VI by the Japanese government and the World Bank etc as a policy framework for the achievement of UHC; hold an international meeting for follow-up the progress of UHC in Tokyo with the World Bank and the WHO.
objective_interpretation: Both policies aim to strengthen public health services and outbreak response capacity. Policy 1 focuses on national and local infection prevention and control and rapid expert deployment to contain antimicrobial-resistant infections, while Policy 2 seeks to bolster the global health architecture, emergency response financing (PEF, CFE), WHO capacities, and UHC/preparedness in developing countries. Together they cumulatively bolster health system readiness against AMR by improving both domestic IPC/outbreak response and the international support framework.
implementation_interpretation: Policy 2's financial contributions to global emergency funds (PEF, CFE), support for WHO's response systems, and collaboration on UHC/preparedness create additional resources, coordination mechanisms, and technical frameworks that facilitate the establishment and strengthening of national outbreak response systems under Policy 1. Policy 1's implementation (expert dispatch and local specialist deployment) has little direct impact on Policy 2's global-level instruments and financing mechanisms.

policy_strategic_objective_2: Promotion of R&D to deal with infectious diseases
policy_specific_actions_1:
Enhance the measures taken by the council to promote public private partnership on antimicrobial resistance 
(AMR) to set R&D priorities and create incentives for R&D, taking into account the frequency of emergence of antimicrobial-resistant organisms(AROs) and needs to obtain medical countermeasures in the shortest period possible
policy_specific_actions_2: Based on the 5th Science and Technology Basic Plan (decided by the Cabinet in January 2016) and the Basic Action Plan for Strengthening Measures on Emerging Infectious Diseases (decided in February 2016), promote basic research into pathogens in collaboration with the counterpart organizations at the overseas research centers in Asia and Africa, including epidemiological studies and research for diagnosis and medical remedies; develop new technologies to contribute to prevention, diagnosis and treatment of infectious diseases towards infection control; and develop highly skilled human resources. Also, for neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), develop methods to prevent, diagnose and cure the diseases including the development of drugs at university and other research facilities in Japan and Africa, work for the practical use of the developed methods in society, and train young African researchers through joint research.
objective_interpretation: Both policies seek to boost investment in research and development to address health threats, pushing the shared driver of limited AMR R&D funding in the same direction. Policy AMR-05 targets antimicrobial resistance specifically by promoting AMR R&D and multi-sector cooperation, while SDG-03 advances R&D for infectious diseases broadly, including diagnostics and treatments. Together they create cumulative benefits by expanding both targeted AMR research and the overall infectious-disease research infrastructure.
implementation_interpretation: AMR-05's public-private partnership framework and R&D priority-setting incentives create a structured platform that can absorb and apply the basic research outputs, technologies, and trained personnel generated under SDG-03. Conversely, SDG-03's investments in foundational pathogen research, technology development, and human resource training supply the scientific expertise and innovations that public-private initiatives under AMR-05 need to translate into medical countermeasures. This bi-directional reinforcement makes each policy easier to implement when the other is in place.

policy_strategic_objective_1:
Reuse Wastewater
Develop the Policies and Guidelines of Waste Management Sector
Maximizing the Use of Treated Wastewater in Agriculture
policy_strategic_objective_2: Control the Air Quality and Emissions From the Source
policy_specific_actions_1:
The initiative aims to expand the reuse of treated water to conserve water resources through both rehabilitating treated water pump stations and establishing distribution networks.
The initiative aims to regulate the waste sector in the Kingdom for all types of waste except for radioactive waste. This will be achieved by introducing executive regulations for developing the waste management sector across the Kingdom and developing guidelines to reach the optimal mechanism for executing each activity of waste management in the Kingdom in a manner that guarantees the promotion of quality services, cost reductions and environmental sustainability. Moreover, the initiative aims to develop governance for processes of waste transportation and the elimination of the waste snooping phenomenon during transportation or disposal at unallocated areas by developing a waste transportation document system.
The initiative aims to divert 80 million cubic meters of treated wastewater into the agriculture sector as well as expanding the utilization of treated water by farmers in areas with lower water supplies. This will be achieved through installation of pump stations, pipeline systems, irrigation networks, and laboratories for measuring the water quality. The initiative contributes to Vision 2030 targets to increase water reuse by 8%, which amounts to 1 billion cubic meters in total.
policy_specific_actions_2: The initiative aims to expand the existing national network to monitor air-borne pollutants across the Kingdom, covering all areas and cities. The completed database will facilitate the issuing of daily reports and warnings about the status of air quality. Further, the initiative will ensure facilities adhere to legislation governing the installation of real-time measurement units, which will be connected to the central control database, allowing updates to standards, monitoring of violations , activation of corrective measures, and contributing to preparing a national emergency plan to deal with cases of air pollution, in cooperation with the relevant bodies.
objective_interpretation: Both policies seek to reduce environmental contamination and degradation--SDG-06 by preventing water and soil pollution through expanded treated-wastewater reuse and robust waste-management governance, and SDG-11 by reducing air pollution via source controls and a real-time monitoring network. They both push the shared driver in the same direction, yielding cumulative environmental benefits.
implementation_interpretation: SDG-06's implementation (rehabilitating pump stations, distribution networks, waste management regulations, transport governance) operates in the water/waste sector, whereas SDG-11's implementation (air-quality monitoring network, real-time emission measurement, compliance enforcement) operates in the air-pollution sector. There is no direct interaction, facilitation, or conflict between their implementation processes.

This initiative aims at implementing the National Strategy for Persons with Disabilities, focusing on: Facilitating the employment of persons with disabilities by amending labour regulations and laws, creating a database, establishing and activating integrated national disability registry in terms of medical, educational, social, and professional evaluation for the purpose of monitoring the number, type, and level of disability cases; developing and activating special programs to increase society’s awareness about the rights of persons with disabilities, as well as the awareness of persons with disabilities; providing vocational qualification for persons with disabilities and concerned parties; focusing on the development and activation of the work programs for persons with mental illnesses and intellectual disabilities; and expanding the employment services in private, public, and third sectors.
objective_interpretation: Both SDG-01 and SDG-10 seek to strengthen social care for vulnerable groups (orphans and persons with disabilities), enhancing their capabilities, rights, community integration, and socio-economic status. By addressing key individual socio-demographic determinants (e.g. poverty, marginalization, access to services), they jointly reduce vulnerabilities that drive inappropriate antimicrobial use and susceptibility to infections, pushing the shared driver in the same favorable direction.
implementation_interpretation: The two policies share nearly identical implementation mechanisms--developing unified business models for orphanages, establishing the Authority for Persons with Disabilities, partnering with private and non-profit sectors, and rolling out integrated e-platforms and national registries. Each policy's rollout directly supports and reinforces the other's actions, creating a positive feedback loop in resource use, stakeholder engagement, and institutional capacity building.

policy_strategic_objective_1: Launch a Comprehensive Program to Spread Digital Awareness, Digital knowledge, and Build National Human Capital to Drive Digital Transformation
policy_strategic_objective_2: Promoting Remote Work
policy_specific_actions_1: This initiative aims to bridge the gap between supply and demand for national talents in the information technology and telecom sectors by developing highly qualified talents. This will be achieved by providing training programs and scholarships across the Kingdom. Additionally, the initiative will increase the availability of technical resources and spread technical awareness.
policy_specific_actions_2: This initiative aims to create a flexible employment method that opens opportunities for more workers to join the national workforce. The initiative targets people who have difficulty attending at the company’s premises. Furthermore, it aims to develop the labor market by creating work opportunities in appropriate, stable, and productive jobs. It will also provide employers with a platform to manage and enable manpower in a more efficient and reliable manner.
objective_interpretation: Both policies act on individual socio-demographic factors by improving digital skills and work flexibility. SDG-04 enhances digital literacy and technical awareness, while SDG-08 expands remote work opportunities. Together they push the same driver in the same direction, cumulatively strengthening individuals' capacity and socioeconomic status, which can help mitigate AMR risk.
implementation_interpretation: Policy 1's training programs, scholarships and expanded technical resources directly equip individuals with the digital skills and readiness required for remote work under Policy 2. Conversely, the new demand for digitally skilled remote workers created by Policy 2 reinforces uptake and support for Policy 1's education and talent-building initiatives, creating a positive feedback loop.

policy_strategic_objective_2: National Strategic Program for Occupational Safety and Health
policy_specific_actions_1: The initiative aims to institute the Saudi Foreign Agricultural Investment Program by satisfying the organizational, technical, and technological requirements to achieve food safety objectives. The initiative includes granting loans in a manner that ensures the desired impact and realization of added value from the program’s finances with the fewest possible risks. This will contribute to addressing the consequences arising from the decision to prevent the planting of certain major grains and crops in order to safeguard water resources.
policy_specific_actions_2:
""This initiative aims to establish regulations, laws, and legislations related to occupational health and safety in the workplace. objective_interpretation: Both policies contribute to improving patient health status--a key driver of AMR--by reducing health risks through different pathways. SDG-02 secures food safety and nutritional quality via foreign agricultural investments and water-sparing crop decisions, while SDG-03 enhances worker health and safety through occupational health regulations and prevention measures. Together, they drive the shared goal of better patient health, reducing infection burdens and subsequent antibiotic use.
implementation_interpretation: SDG-02 is implemented through agricultural-investment financing, technology and organizational requirements for food safety, whereas SDG-03 is implemented via occupational health regulations, awareness campaigns and workplace inspections. They involve different authorities, funding streams and action areas, with no apparent facilitation or interference between them.

implementation_interpretation: Policy 1's actions (skills training, job placement, housing support) do not facilitate or hinder the technical and capital works of water provision, irrigation, and sanitation expansion in Policy 2. Likewise, enhanced water and sanitation services do not materially ease or obstruct orphan empowerment activities. There is no direct interaction between the two implementation streams.

policy_strategic_objective_1:
Parallel Training to Meet Labor Market Requirements
Provide Childcare Services for Working Women
policy_strategic_objective_2: Incentivize Employers to Develop Suitable Environments for Persons with Disabilities (Mowaamah Program)
policy_specific_actions_1:
This initiative is aimed at developing training programs targeting unemployed women. The program consists of on-the-job training (by the employer) in parallel with a training program (technical and personal skills) by specialized training authorities. Upon training completion, the female trainee obtains an approved certificate from the training program owner. Furthermore, participating companies will be supported in various ways.
This initiative aims to empower Saudi working women to join the labor market while being reassured regarding the care provided to their children during their work period. Saudi working women will be able to enroll their their children in any childcare service centers licensed by “Qurrah” e-system.
policy_specific_actions_2: This initiative aims at developing work environment standards for persons with disabilities and make it available electronically via mowaamah platform.
objective_interpretation: Both policies seek to dismantle social-cultural barriers to labor market participation--Policy 1 by empowering women through training and childcare support, and Policy 2 by creating inclusive workplace standards for persons with disabilities. Together they promote broader social inclusion and equity, addressing the same social-cultural drivers of AMR related to exclusion and uneven access to resources and decision-making.
implementation_interpretation: The childcare and training infrastructure for women (Qurrah e-system and on-the-job training scheme) does not directly affect the development or uptake of electronic work-environment standards for persons with disabilities (Mowaamah), nor vice versa. There is no clear overlap or mutual influence between the two implementation mechanisms.
